In confirmatione autem regulae ordinis fratrum Minorum Honorii III., Gregorii IX., Innocentii IV., Alexandri IV., Nicolai IV., praedecessorum nostrorum summorum Pontificum, haec verba asserunt contineri: „Haec est regula evangelica Christi, et Apostolorum imitatrix, quae nihil in hoc mundo habet proprium vel commune, sed in rebus, quibus utuntur, habent simplicem usum facti:“ his addere praesumentes, praefatos summos Pontifices et multa concilia generalia per clavem scientiae diffinisse, paupertatem Christi et Apostolorum constitisse perfecte in expropriatione cuiuslibet temporalis dominii civilis et mundani, et sustentationem eorum in solo et nudo usu facti etiam constitisse, ex quibus nituntur concludere, non licuisse nec licere ipsorum successoribus contra praemissa aliquid immutare. Ideoque quum constitutio nostra in ratione praedicta contra diffinitiones praedictorum praedecessorum nostrorum (sicut asserunt) diffinierit, Christum et Apostolos in iis, quae habuerunt, habuisse non tantum simplicem usum facti, sed ius faciendi de ipsis, eosque ipsos fecisse scriptura sacra testatur, pertinacem assertionem dicentium, ipsos ius huiusmodi minime habuisse, quum actus illorum fuisse concludant non iustos, quod de Christo nefas est dicere, haereticam declarando: concludere satagunt, licet falso, nobis non licuisse declarare vel statuere supra dicta. Item, quia constitutio: „Ad conditorem canonum,“ contra diffinitiones praedictas fratres Minores asserit non posse habere in re aliqua simplicem usum facti: nituntur similiter concludere contra ipsam.
units.en: To attack the said constitutions they have used publicly, it is reported, both in word and in writing, the following argument. What the Roman pontiffs have once defined in faith and morals by the key of knowledge (clavem scientiae), they say, remains so unchangeable that a successor may not call it in question or affirm the contrary, although they admit it is otherwise with what they have ordained by the key of power (clavem potestatis). And in the confirmation of the rule of the order of Friars Minor by Honorius III, Gregory IX, Innocent IV, Alexander IV and Nicholas IV, our predecessors as supreme pontiffs, they assert that these words are contained: 'This is the evangelical rule of Christ, imitating the apostles, which has nothing in this world of its own or in common, but in the things they use they have the simple use of fact'; and they presume to add that those supreme pontiffs and many general councils defined by the key of knowledge that the poverty of Christ and the apostles consisted perfectly in the renunciation of all temporal ownership, civil and worldly, and that their sustenance too consisted in the sole and bare use of fact; from which they try to conclude that it was not and is not lawful for their successors to change anything against this. And therefore, since our constitution in the said argument (as they assert) defined, against the definitions of our said predecessors, that Christ and the apostles had in what they had not only the simple use of fact but also the right of dealing with it, and that scripture testifies that they did so, declaring heretical the pertinacious assertion of those who say they had no such right, since it concludes that their acts were not just, which it is wicked to say of Christ: they strive to conclude, though falsely, that it was not lawful for us to declare or ordain the foregoing. Likewise, since the constitution 'Ad conditorem canonum' asserts, against the said definitions, that the Friars Minor cannot have a simple use of fact in any thing, they try to conclude similarly against it.
units.note: Both OCRs of the reprint read 'elavem' for clavem; the page reads clavem. Friedberg again prints 'Nicolai IV.' where his manuscripts read III. The formula the friars quote echoes Nicholas III's Exiit qui seminat. The distinction between the 'key of knowledge' and the 'key of power' is the friars' strongest argument, and the one John XXII spends the rest of the decretal refuting: if what one pope has defined in faith cannot be revoked by another, John XXII himself was a heretic. The argument has been read by modern historians as an early form of the doctrine of papal infallibility, turned here against a pope.

units.titel: The pope's answer, in one sentence
units.orig: Quod autem, quod in ratione praedicta praemittitur, videlicet, quod illa, quae per clavem scientiae in fide ac moribus a summis Pontificibus semel sunt diffinita, eorum successoribus revocare non licet in dubium, nec contrarium affirmare, licet secus sit (sicut dicunt) in iis, quae per clavem potestatis per summos Pontifices ordinantur, prorsus sit contrarium veritati, patet ex sequentibus evidenter. […]
units.en: But that what is put first in the said argument, namely that what has once been defined by the supreme pontiffs in faith and morals by the key of knowledge may not be called in question by their successors, nor the contrary affirmed, although it is otherwise (as they say) with what is ordained by the supreme pontiffs by the key of power, is wholly contrary to the truth, is plain from what follows. […]
units.note: The long refutation that follows (cols. 1231–1236: the key of knowledge is no key at all, the rule's confirmations were not definitions of faith, popes have revoked their predecessors' acts before) is not yet carried.

units.orig: […] Nos itaque, ne fabricatores mendaciorum huiusmodi ac etiam assertores de tam pestifera, erronea et damnata doctrina, confutatione ac confusione utique omni digna, gloriari valeant et alios trahere in errorem, quum ausu arreptando ac petulantia improba ausi defendere publice fuerint damnatam per constitutionem praedictam haeresin ac etiam probare, videlicet quod Christus et eius apostoli in iis, quae habuisse leguntur, tantum habuerint absque iure aliquo simplicem usum facti, ex quo (si verum esset) sequeretur, usum Christi fuisse non iustum, quod profecto blasphemiam continet, et catholicae fidei inimicum, quum hoc de pertinaci animositate ac erronea non sit dubium processisse, omnes et singulos, qui verbo ac scripto per se vel alium seu alios talia publice praesumpserunt, ipsos quoque, qui eos docuerunt in talibus et ut praemissa facerent, in damnatam incidisse haeresin, ac ut haereticos evitandos fore, de fratrum nostrorum consilio declaramus. Si quis autem damnatas per constitutionem: „Quum inter praedictam,“ haereses, vel ipsarum alteram, deinceps scienter verbo vel scripto defendere vel approbare praesumpserit: de fratrum eorundem consilio decernimus, ut tanquam haereticus ab omnibus evidenter habeatur. Adhuc quod constitutionem nostram: „Ad conditorem canonum,“ supra dictam insano ausu impugnare nisi sunt, sicut fertur, districtius de eorundem fratrum consilio inhibemus, ne quisquam contra diffinita, ordinata seu facta per ipsam, verbo vel scripto scienter approbet aliquid vel defendat. Si quis vero contra praesumpserit, tanquam contumax et rebellis Romanae ecclesiae ab omnibus habeatur. Nulli ergo etc. Data Avinion. IV. Idus Novembris Pont. nostri Ao. IX. [1324.]
units.en: […] We therefore, lest the fabricators of such lies, and the defenders of so pestilent, erroneous and condemned a doctrine, worthy of all refutation and confusion, may boast and draw others into error, since with seizing boldness and wicked petulance they have dared publicly to defend, and even to prove, the heresy condemned by the said constitution, namely that Christ and his apostles, in what they are read to have had, had only a simple use of fact without any right, from which (were it true) it would follow that Christ's use was unjust, which is plainly blasphemous and hostile to the catholic faith; since there is no doubt that this proceeded from pertinacious and erroneous animosity: we declare, on the advice of our brothers, that all and each who have presumed such things publicly, by word and writing, themselves or through another or others, and those too who taught them in such things and to do the foregoing, have fallen into the condemned heresy and are to be avoided as heretics. And if anyone henceforth knowingly presumes to defend or approve by word or writing the heresies condemned by the said constitution 'Quum inter', or either of them, we decree on the advice of the same brothers that he be held by all as plainly a heretic. Further, since they have tried, it is reported, with insane boldness to attack our constitution 'Ad conditorem canonum' mentioned above, we strictly forbid, on the advice of the same brothers, that anyone knowingly approve or defend anything by word or writing against what is defined, ordained or done by it. If anyone presumes otherwise, let him be held by all as contumacious and a rebel against the Roman Church. Let no man, then, etc. Given at Avignon on the fourth day before the Ides of November, in the ninth year of our pontificate [1324].
units.note: 10 November 1324. With this sentence the Franciscan position became heresy for anyone who went on defending it. Michael of Cesena kept the order formally obedient until he was summoned to Avignon in 1327; the break came in April and May 1328 (Appeal [3], Chron. Flight [1]). The printed 'Quum inter praedictam' is Friedberg's text: the constitution meant is Quum inter nonnullos.
